item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"medium","summary":"A is the preferable review candidate because its extra retry change is narrower and its retry test verifies the multipart payload on every attempt. Neither patch is merge-ready: both violate the contract by reimplementing FilesService.Add inside Upload instead of delegating to Add.","reasons":["Both Upload implementations correctly validate inputs, use multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", preserve FilesOption data, and propagate encoding errors.","A verifies the multipart filename, field, content, and replayed content across the 429 retry; B's Upload retry test only drains the body and would not detect corrupted or empty retried multipart content.","A limits its out-of-scope RawClient behavior change to seekable readers. B eagerly buffers every non-native reader across RawClient.Do whenever WithNoRetry is absent, creating a much broader memory, latency, streaming, and error-timing change.","B does provide the explicitly requested source-reader-error test and better direct option coverage, but that test-quality advantage does not outweigh its substantially broader production behavior change."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), contrary to the frozen contract and creating future divergence risk.","The source-reader failure path is not tested as explicitly required.","wireSeekableRequestBody is an unrelated retry refactor and changes body ownership by preventing the transport from closing caller-provided seekable bodies. It also mutates the reader while probing its size and can leave it at the end if restoring the original offset fails."],"risks_b":["Upload duplicates Add rather than routing through it, violating a central contract requirement.","RawClient.Do now reads arbitrary reader bodies fully into memory even when the configured policy would not retry that method, materially changing generic request behavior beyond the requested Files API work.","Buffering changes streaming, source-reader consumption and closure behavior, and when read errors surface; WithNoRetry becomes necessary merely to retain prior streaming behavior, expanding API semantics outside scope scope discipline requires."]}
